Addressed every open item in the review of `7010ba500068cff1d49f9e211873871107b16008`:

1. **HTTP revalidation** ([shared finisher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed77b3583db8e57dc9d562ee95dce78208470fc6/src/gateway/http-request-authority.ts#L133)): the shared response finisher recognizes unavailable authority, returns 503 with `retryable: false` after a possible side effect, and closes already-started responses. The real-server core/plugin cases fail before this repair (500 rather than 503) and pass afterward; the live grant remains active.
2. **Plugin cookies** ([cookie owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed77b3583db8e57dc9d562ee95dce78208470fc6/src/gateway/http-auth-plugin-cookie.ts#L123)): cookie admission sends the shared 503 response, and revalidation without a response object propagates the typed unavailable error to its outer response owner. The regression fails before the repair (401 rather than 503); all 14 cookie tests pass afterward, including genuine revocation and independent owner credentials.
3. **Visitor denials** ([visitor owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed77b3583db8e57dc9d562ee95dce78208470fc6/extensions/visitor-access/src/visitors.ts#L92)): the bundled visitor owner returns `undefined` for an absent invitation, which the existing required-role binding denies. Service startup and internal evaluation errors still throw. Consumer fixtures now express actual absent/aborted grants instead of treating generic exceptions as denials.
4. **Extracted wrapper** ([inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ed77b3583db8e57dc9d562ee95dce78208470fc6/scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt#L1197)): added `src/infra/operator-authority-error.ts` to the existing wrapper inventory. This fixes the missing import reported by the closure and provisioning tests.

The earlier unsafe-retry and HTTP-authentication items remain fixed: only failures before actual handler execution promise a retry, and HTTP policy outages are distinct from invalid credentials. The regression for closed invocation scopes retains the same admitted descendants and model authority through failure and recovery, then proves that genuine revocation still stops them.

Final repair head: `ed77b3583db8e57dc9d562ee95dce78208470fc6`. The two extraction cases and two applicable originally failing provisioning cases pass in the frozen replay. The separate macOS sparse-provisioning timeout remains recorded in the PR evidence and is not claimed as inherited.
